A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoSEP and retain the same central algorithm, datasets, and main experiments. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments across eight tasks and three MLLMs, together with correlation, learning-dynamics, sample-size, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds comparator results, a sampling ablation, and experiments with additional model configurations in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: The central algorithm and scoring objective are unchanged. Appendix D.2 adds a hybrid adaptation: Gemini 1.5 Flash generates descriptions and performs reflection and modification, while Qwen2-VL-7B handles instance-level classification and evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight subsets of CUB-200-2011, iNaturalist 2021, Stanford Dogs, and VegFru. The new appendix experiments reuse existing classification tasks; additional models and sampling controls do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Few-shot with MLLM labels across all eight tasks and three original models. The existing comparator identities are retained, including Multiple images display, whose scores are revised and whose attribution is added.

E3.justification: Appendices C.3 and D introduce same-class versus different-class sampling controls, Gemini 2.0 Flash evaluations, and a Gemini-assisted Qwen2-VL-7B configuration. No change to the original test splits or accuracy metric is established. The new class-balance statement documents an existing setting without establishing rebalancing.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a focused ablation of instance-level sampling on CUB_cuckoo with Gemini 1.5 Flash. Table 3 compares same-class, different-class, and random sampling and reports similar accuracies. Existing learning-dynamics, sample-size, correlation, diversity, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report variability alongside accuracy and retain the three independent learning-dynamics runs described in Appendix C.1. Added tables follow the existing reporting convention; no new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are specified.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds 24 self-labeled few-shot results and replaces all 24 Multiple images display results, materially changing some rankings. For Qwen2-VL on CUB_cuckoo, the latter entry changes from 60.73% to 65.12%, exceeding AutoSEP's unchanged 63.41%. Tables 3–5 add sampling and model findings, including 69.05% for Gemini 2.0 Flash on CUB_vireo and 61.79% for the hybrid 7B setup on CUB_cuckoo. Original AutoSEP scores, other existing comparator scores, and Table 2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix F specifies the diversity metric's previously unspecified maximum-based normalization and additive combination in Equations 7–8. Section 4.3 adds query-complexity expressions for optimization baselines. AutoSEP's existing mathematical formulation is retained, with equation renumbering but no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and Section 4.2 narrow the claimed average advantage over the best-performing baselines from 5% to 3%. The claimed 13% improvement over vanilla zero-shot and the central unsupervised, black-box contribution remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly explains why same-class image pairs can encourage detailed, discriminative descriptions. Appendix D.2 explicitly identifies dependence on a strong model for generation and refinement while interpreting hybrid results as applicability to smaller MLLMs. The original limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies class-balanced evaluation, five majority votes per optimization update, baseline query costs, the hybrid model-role assignment, and the exact diversity-score calculation. Hardware and code-access information remain unchanged. Existing prompt templates move from Appendix D to E.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Jiang et al.'s many-shot in-context learning, Promptomatix, and the Gemini 2.5 report. It newly attributes Multiple images display to Jiang et al. and connects the hybrid setup to prior prompt-optimization practice. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains verbatim. Changes include updated author and conference information, acknowledgments, localized experimental explanations, new appendix subsections, and renaming Prompt Details from Appendix D to E. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains comparator rows and a model-name clarification; three compact appendix tables are added. The author block is compressed, Algorithm 1 is relocated, and appendix material reflows. Existing figures and their plotted content are retained without substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical scrutiny through a self-labeled few-shot comparator, a sampling control, and additional model evaluations, while making costs and the diversity metric more explicit. The reduced headline margin better reflects the revised comparisons. Gains remain limited: blanket outperformance wording still conflicts with Table 1, and the smaller-model evidence depends on Gemini assistance rather than demonstrating independent 7B capability.
